cases.sentence: Дуня улыбнулась и протянула ему руку, но ___ не сходила с ее лица.
cases.translation: Dunya smiled and held out her hand to him, but worry did not leave her face.
cases.explain: "Забота" is the subject of the verb "не сходила" (did not leave), so it stands in the nominative case.

cases.sentence: Дуня улыбнулась и протянула ему руку, но забота не сходила с ее ___.
cases.translation: Dunya smiled and held out her hand to him, but worry did not leave her face.
cases.explain: The preposition "с" (from/off) governs the genitive case here, giving "лица."

cases.sentence: Странно предположить, чтоб он так глупо приступил к ___, если б имел на тебя дурные намерения.
cases.translation: It's strange to suppose he would go about the matter so foolishly if he had bad intentions toward you.
cases.explain: The verb phrase "приступить к" (to set about/get down to) governs the dative case, giving "делу."

cases.translation: Dunya smiled and held out her hand to him.
cases.explain: "Руку" is the direct object of the transitive verb "протянула" (held out), so it takes the accusative case.

cases.sentence: Горячо прошептал Разумихин над самым ее ___, крепко стиснув ей руку.
cases.translation: Razumikhin whispered fervently right by her ear, gripping her hand tightly.
cases.explain: The preposition "над" (above/over) governs the instrumental case, giving "ухом."

cases.sentence: Здесь есть одна квартира, в этом же ___, от тех же хозяев.
cases.translation: There's an apartment here, in this very same building, from the same landlords.
cases.explain: The preposition "в" (in), indicating static location, governs the prepositional case, giving "доме."

cases.translation: Raskolnikov was waiting for him at the end of the corridor.
cases.explain: The noun "конец" (end), used to indicate a part of something, governs the genitive case, giving "коридора."

cases.sentence: Раскольников с болезненно искривившимся ___ сказал: «Понимаешь теперь?..»
cases.translation: Raskolnikov, his face twisted with pain, said: "Do you understand now?.."
cases.explain: The preposition "с" (with) governs the instrumental case here, giving "лицом."

reading.ru: Главное дело было в том, что он, до самой последней минуты, никак не ожидал подобной развязки.
reading.question: What was Luzhin's main problem, according to the narrator, right up until the last minute?
options: He never expected such an outcome to the confrontation
He expected Raskolnikov to leave first
reading.correct: He never expected such an outcome to the confrontation
reading.explain: The narrator states that Luzhin, until the very last minute, simply did not expect such a resolution to the scene.

reading.ru: Дуня же была ему просто необходима; отказаться от нее для него было немыслимо.
reading.question: How essential was Dunya to Luzhin's plans, according to the narrator?
options: She was simply indispensable to him; giving her up was unthinkable
She was just one option among many for him
He had already decided to give her up before the scene
She meant nothing to his future plans
reading.correct: She was simply indispensable to him; giving her up was unthinkable
reading.explain: The narrator explains that Dunya was simply indispensable to Luzhin; renouncing her was unthinkable for him.

reading.ru: — Нет, я, я более всех виновата! — говорила Дунечка, обнимая и целуя мать, — я польстилась на его деньги, но, клянусь, брат, — я и не воображала, чтоб это был такой недостойный человек.
reading.question: What does Dunechka insist while embracing and kissing her mother after Luzhin leaves?
options: That she herself is more to blame than anyone
That her mother is entirely at fault
That Raskolnikov is to blame for everything
reading.correct: That she herself is more to blame than anyone
reading.explain: Dunechka insists, while embracing her mother, that she herself is more to blame than anyone for what happened.

reading.ru: Все радовались, через пять минут даже смеялись.
reading.question: How does the family's mood shift shortly after Luzhin's departure?
options: Everyone rejoices, and within five minutes they are even laughing
They immediately begin packing to leave
reading.correct: Everyone rejoices, and within five minutes they are even laughing
reading.explain: The text says everyone was glad, and within five minutes they were even laughing.

reading.ru: Раскольников поднял голову.
reading.question: What does Raskolnikov do when Dunya and her mother ask what Svidrigailov said to him?
options: He raises his head to answer
He refuses to answer at all
He asks Razumikhin to explain instead
reading.correct: He raises his head to answer
reading.explain: The text shows Raskolnikov raising his head before answering their question about Svidrigailov.

reading.ru: — Видеть! Ни за что на свете! — вскричала Пульхерия Александровна, — и как он смеет ей деньги предлагать!
reading.question: How does Pulkheria Alexandrovna react to the idea of Dunya meeting Svidrigailov?
options: She cries out that it must never happen, and is outraged he'd offer money
She calmly agrees it might be useful
She asks Dunya to decide for herself
She suggests inviting him to dinner
reading.correct: She cries out that it must never happen, and is outraged he'd offer money
reading.explain: Pulkheria Alexandrovna exclaims that Dunya must never see him, and is indignant that he dares offer her money.

reading.ru: Тогда он объявил, что будет сам, всеми средствами, доискиваться свидания.
reading.question: What did Svidrigailov say he would do if Raskolnikov refused to pass along his message?
options: He would seek a meeting with Dunya by every means himself
He would go to the police instead
He would give up on the idea entirely
reading.correct: He would seek a meeting with Dunya by every means himself
reading.explain: Raskolnikov reports that Svidrigailov declared he would seek a personal meeting with Dunya by every possible means.

reading.ru: Ну что бы с нами было теперь, Дуня, без этих трех тысяч!
reading.question: What does Pulkheria Alexandrovna exclaim about the significance of the three thousand rubles?
options: That she doesn't know what they would have done without that money
That it is not enough to matter
That it should be returned to Svidrigailov
That Luzhin deserves credit for it
reading.correct: That she doesn't know what they would have done without that money
reading.explain: Pulkheria Alexandrovna exclaims in relief, wondering what would have become of them without those three thousand rubles.

reading.ru: — Он что-нибудь ужасное задумал! — проговорила она почти шепотом про себя, чуть не содрогаясь.
reading.question: What does Dunya fear about Svidrigailov's intentions?
options: That he has planned something terrible
That he plans to marry someone else
That he plans to leave the country soon
That he plans to visit Porfiry
reading.correct: That he has planned something terrible
reading.explain: Dunya murmurs almost in a whisper, nearly shuddering, that Svidrigailov must have planned something terrible.

reading.ru: Будем следить! Я его выслежу! — энергически крикнул Разумихин.
reading.question: What does Razumikhin vow to do regarding Svidrigailov?
options: To watch and track him down
To confront him violently at once
To write a letter of complaint
To ask Porfiry to arrest him
reading.correct: To watch and track him down
reading.explain: Razumikhin energetically vows that they will keep watch and that he will track Svidrigailov down.

reading.ru: Ораторствовал Разумихин.
reading.question: Who dominates the lively conversation a quarter of an hour later?
options: Razumikhin, who holds forth like an orator
reading.correct: Razumikhin, who holds forth like an orator
reading.explain: The text notes plainly that Razumikhin was the one orating/holding forth in the conversation.

reading.ru: Тут Разумихин принялся развивать свой проект и много толковал о том, как почти все наши книгопродавцы и издатели мало знают толку в своем товаре, а потому обыкновенно и плохие издатели, между тем как порядочные издания вообще окупаются и дают процент, иногда значительный.
reading.question: What does Razumikhin begin to elaborate on enthusiastically?
options: His plan for a publishing business
His plan to become a lawyer
His plan to join the police
reading.correct: His plan for a publishing business
reading.explain: Razumikhin sets about elaborating his project, a publishing venture, discussing book dealers and editors.

reading.ru: — То, что вы говорите, мне очень нравится, Дмитрий Прокофьич, — сказала она.
reading.question: How does Dunya respond to Razumikhin's publishing proposal?
options: She says she likes very much what he is saying
She says she needs more time to think
She defers entirely to her brother's opinion
reading.correct: She says she likes very much what he is saying
reading.explain: Dunya tells Razumikhin directly that what he is saying pleases her very much.

reading.ru: — Как ты думаешь, брат? — сказала Дуня.
reading.question: Whose opinion does Dunya seek about Razumikhin's publishing plan?
reading.correct: Her brother Raskolnikov's opinion
reading.explain: Dunya turns and asks her brother directly what he thinks of the plan.

reading.ru: — Ура! — закричал Разумихин, — теперь стойте, здесь есть одна квартира, в этом же доме, от тех же хозяев.
reading.question: How does Razumikhin react when he thinks of an available apartment for the family?
options: He argues that it's a bad idea
reading.correct: He shouts "Hurrah!"
reading.explain: Razumikhin exclaims "Hurrah!" as he remembers a suitable apartment in the same building.

reading.ru: Дуня смотрела на брата с недоверчивым удивлением.
reading.question: How does Dunya react as she watches Raskolnikov prepare to leave suddenly?
reading.correct: With disbelieving astonishment
reading.explain: The text describes Dunya looking at her brother with distrustful, disbelieving surprise as he prepares to leave.

reading.ru: — А ведь кто знает, может, и последний раз видимся, — прибавил он нечаянно.
reading.question: What unsettling remark does Raskolnikov accidentally blurt out to his family?
options: That this might be the last time they see each other
That he plans to marry soon
reading.correct: That this might be the last time they see each other
reading.explain: Raskolnikov adds, almost involuntarily, that this might be the last time they see one another.

reading.ru: Но в бледном лице его была какая-то резкая решимость.
reading.question: What does the narrator note about Raskolnikov's pale face as he prepares to explain himself?
options: It showed a sharp, stark determination
reading.correct: It showed a sharp, stark determination
reading.explain: The narrator observes that his pale face bore a certain sharp, stark determination.

reading.ru: И мать, и сестра были в страшном испуге; Разумихин тоже.
reading.question: How do Raskolnikov's mother, sister, and Razumikhin react to his announcement that he wants to be left alone?
options: All three are thrown into terrible fright
Only his mother is upset, the others are calm
They laugh, thinking he is joking
reading.correct: All three are thrown into terrible fright
reading.explain: The text says both his mother and sister were in terrible fright, and so was Razumikhin.

reading.ru: — Брат! Что ты с матерью делаешь! — прошептала она со взглядом, горевшим от негодования.
reading.question: What does Dunya whisper to Raskolnikov as she catches up to him at the door?
options: A reproach about what he is doing to their mother
A plea for him to marry Razumikhin's friend's sister
reading.correct: A reproach about what he is doing to their mother
reading.explain: Dunya whispers reproachfully, asking what he is doing to their mother, her eyes burning with indignation.

reading.ru: — Бесчувственный, злобный эгоист! — вскрикнула Дуня.
reading.question: What harsh accusation does Dunya throw at her brother as he walks away?
options: That he is a callous, malicious egotist
reading.correct: That he is a callous, malicious egotist
reading.explain: Dunya cries out that he is a callous, spiteful egotist as he leaves the room.

reading.ru: Раскольников поджидал его в конце коридора.
reading.question: Where is Raskolnikov waiting for Razumikhin after he runs out of the room?
options: At the end of the corridor
By the front door of the building
reading.correct: At the end of the corridor
reading.explain: The text states plainly that Raskolnikov was waiting for him at the end of the corridor.

reading.ru: Да куда ты? Что ты? Да что с тобой? Да разве можно так!..
reading.question: What does the bewildered Razumikhin mutter as Raskolnikov walks away from him without a handshake?
options: A string of confused questions about where he's going and what's wrong
An angry demand for an explanation
A joke to lighten the mood
reading.correct: A string of confused questions about where he's going and what's wrong
reading.explain: The utterly bewildered Razumikhin mutters a series of anxious questions about where Raskolnikov is going and what's wrong.

reading.ru: Разумихин всю жизнь помнил эту минуту.
reading.question: How significant is the silent moment between Raskolnikov and Razumikhin in the dark corridor?
options: Razumikhin remembers that moment for the rest of his life
It is quickly forgotten by both of them
It only matters to Raskolnikov, not Razumikhin
It is described as entirely unremarkable
reading.correct: Razumikhin remembers that moment for the rest of his life
reading.explain: The narrator states that Razumikhin remembered that minute for his whole life.

reading.ru: Одним словом, с этого вечера Разумихин стал у них сыном и братом.
reading.question: What role does Razumikhin take on for Raskolnikov's mother and sister from that evening onward?
options: He becomes like a son and brother to them
He becomes their financial advisor only
He distances himself from the family
reading.correct: He becomes like a son and brother to them
reading.explain: The narrator concludes that from that evening on, Razumikhin became like a son and a brother to them.

highlight.question: Which sentence conveys the devastating impact of the rupture on the character?
sentences: Как нарочно, незадолго перед тем, после долгих соображений и ожиданий, он решил наконец окончательно переменить карьеру и вступить в более обширный круг деятельности, а с тем вместе, мало-помалу, перейти и в более высшее общество, о котором он давно уже с сладострастием подумывал…
Одним словом, он решился попробовать Петербурга.
Он знал, что женщинами можно «весьма и весьма» много выиграть.
Обаяние прелестной, добродетельной и образованной женщины могло удивительно скрасить его дорогу, привлечь к нему, создать ореол…  и вот всё рушилось!
Этот теперешний внезапный, безобразный разрыв подействовал на него как удар грома.
highlight.explain: This sentence describes how the sudden, ugly rupture affected him like a thunderbolt, emphasizing the shock of his plans collapsing.

highlight.question: Which sentences reveal Razumikhin's overwhelming emotional response to the situation?
sentences: Но Разумихин был в восторге.
Он не смел еще вполне его выразить, но весь дрожал как в лихорадке, как будто пятипудовая гиря свалилась с его сердца.
Теперь он имеет право отдать им всю свою жизнь, служить им…
Да мало ли что теперь!
А впрочем, он еще пугливее гнал дальнейшие мысли и боялся своего воображения.
highlight.explain: These sentences show that Razumikhin was in rapture and trembling as if with fever, with a great weight lifted from his heart.

highlight.question: Which sentences express how critical the three thousand rubles were to the family's survival?
sentences: — Упокой, господи, ее душу!
— воскликнула Пульхерия Александровна, — вечно, вечно за нее бога буду молить!
Ну что бы с нами было теперь, Дуня, без этих трех тысяч!
Господи, точно с неба упали!

Ах, Родя, ведь у нас утром всего три целковых за душой оставалось, и мы с Дунечкой только и рассчитывали, как бы часы где-нибудь поскорей заложить, чтобы не брать только у этого, пока сам не догадается.
highlight.explain: These sentences show that without this money the family would not have known what to do, and just that morning they had almost nothing and were considering pawning their watch.

highlight.question: Which sentence introduces Razumikhin's concrete plan for a business enterprise?
sentences: Ну, хоть некоторое время…
Меня же возьмите в друзья, в компаньоны, и уж уверяю, что затеем отличное предприятие.
Слушайте, я вам в подробности это всё растолкую — весь проект!
У меня еще утром, когда ничего еще не случилось, в голове уж мелькало…
Вот в чем дело: есть у меня дядя (я вас познакомлю; прескладной и препочтенный старичонка!), а у этого дяди есть тысяча рублей капиталу, а сам живет пенсионом и не нуждается.
highlight.explain: This sentence presents the practical foundation of his proposal, mentioning his uncle who has capital available for investment.

highlight.question: Which sentences express cautious optimism about the feasibility of the publishing enterprise?
sentences: — Я думаю, что у него очень хорошая мысль, — ответил он.
— О фирме, разумеется, мечтать заранее не надо, но пять-шесть книг действительно можно издать с несомненным успехом.
Я и сам знаю одно сочинение, которое непременно пойдет.
А что касается до того, что он сумеет повести дело, так в этом нет и сомнения: дело смыслит…
Впрочем, будет еще время вам сговориться…
highlight.explain: These sentences indicate that while they shouldn't plan too far ahead, five or six books could definitely be published successfully and Razumikhin knows of at least one work that will succeed.

highlight.question: Which sentences express Razumikhin's passionate defense of the character's mental state?
sentences: — Он су-ма-сшедший, а не бесчувственный!
Он помешанный!
Неужели вы этого не видите?
Вы бесчувственная после этого!..
— горячо прошептал Разумихин над самым ее ухом, крепко стиснув ей руку.
highlight.explain: These sentences assert that the person is mad rather than callous, conveying Razumikhin's emotional intensity in explaining the character's condition.
